problems.source_says: The original DAT averages semantic distances among the ten nouns generated by the same participant. Under the codebook rule that variety among one person's own ideas is flexibility, this is flexibility rather than overall_creativity; it is not diversity across people. The paper describes it as a divergent-thinking measure and an indicator of creative potential.
problems.quote: In the Divergent Association Task, participants were asked to generate 10 nouns that were as diﬀerent from each other as possible in all meanings and uses of the words, in Chinese.
problems.locator: PDF pp. 16-17, Appendices A.2 and B.1; creativity-codebook.md, Section 6, Construct

problems.source_says: The original-DAT component has the same within-person variety construct as S1-O4 and should be flexibility under the codebook. The modified DAT instead averages six supplied-word/response distances; the two are separate scores in Figure 4b, not one composite. Separate the measures so that the original DAT can receive its appropriate construct.
problems.quote: In the Divergent Association Task, participants were asked to generate 10 nouns that were as diﬀerent from each other as possible in all meanings and uses of the words, in Chinese.
problems.locator: PDF pp. 16-17, Appendices A.2 and B.1; p. 11, Figure 4b; creativity-codebook.md, Section 6, Construct

problems.source_says: The saved PDF establishes post-task testing after Questionnaire II, but does not explicitly state that ChatGPT was unavailable or removed during either repeated DAT. Table 1 labels access for the picture tasks and leaves the DAT access status unspecified. Post-treatment timing alone does not establish after_ai, which requires AI removal. These two fields remain unconfirmed from this document; this is an evidence gap, not evidence that AI was available. The separate supplementary instructions are not in the supplied PDF.

problems.form_value: Fig. 4b plots the coefficient with its 95% CI; no number is printed. Read from the figure (approximate): HAT estimate below zero, about -0.5 points, with the CI reaching zero. Text: 'their effect on the DAT score are not statistically significant.'
problems.source_says: The form's approximately -0.5-point HAT estimate is a visual approximation. Figure 4b has no numerical coefficient or interval labels; Section 3.4 reports that the DAT effect is not statistically significant. The form labels its approximation honestly and the graphical direction is consistent, but this is not an exact source-reported number. Under this audit's no-guess rule, retain figure_only and leave the exact raw coefficient and SE null.

problems.source_says: Table 8 reports two additional outcomes derived from creativity ratings of the same produced ideas: an indicator that the image-text grade exceeds the text-only grade, and the image-text minus text-only grade difference. HAT versus Control is 0.075* (SE 0.038) for the indicator's average marginal effect and 0.118** (SE 0.053) for the grade difference; both models have 548 observations. These are secondary with_ai outcomes computed from output ratings, not self-reports. Neither is an outcome record; the form's notes explicitly exclude the gap. The table describes individual/team-idea observations and models analogous to Table 3 columns 2 and 5, so 548 is not a participant count.
problems.quote: we construct a dummy variable indicating whether an idea received an image-text grade that is higher than its text-only grade
problems.locator: PDF p. 14, Table 8 columns 1-2 and Section 4.3

problems.source_says: The same two output-derived outcomes are also reported for Training versus Control: average marginal effect 0.145*** (SE 0.043) for image-text > text-only and coefficient 0.171** (SE 0.069) for image-text minus text-only. Each model has 548 observations. These secondary with_ai outcomes are absent from the Training outcome records and should retain the form's non-randomized cross-wave qualification.
problems.quote: as well as another variable indicating the diﬀerence between the image-text grade and the text-only grade for an idea.
problems.locator: PDF p. 14, Table 8 columns 1-2 and Section 4.3; p. 3, Training comparison qualification

confirmed.statement: Criterion 3 holds: independent student evaluators scored the creativity of submitted ideas; the text-only evaluations directly score participants' own output.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 2, Introduction; p. 6, Section 2.2; p. 7, Section 3.2

confirmed.statement: S1-O1/S1-O2 and S2-O1/S2-O2 use overall creativity grades from 30 student raters per theme on a 1-10 scale; human_raters and scored_on_output are supported.
HAT and Training had ChatGPT during production of the picture ideas in tasks 2-3; with_ai is supported for their grade and grade-inequality outcomes.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Table 1 and Section 2.1; p. 5, Training procedures

confirmed.statement: Image-text ratings are primary; the same evaluators also rated text alone, with counterbalanced evaluation order. The four alpha values in the form match.
All Table 2 means, SDs, standardized values and submission counts quoted in S1-O1/S1-O2/S2-O1/S2-O2 match the PDF.
All quoted Table 3 HAT and Training coefficients, SEs, significance stars and model Ns match; the quoted HHT coefficient 0.307 (0.066) also matches.

The grade analysis is at the idea level. The form correctly discloses expansion of HHT ideas to participant-idea rows in adjusted models and distinguishes unique submission counts from pooled model Ns.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 7-8, Section 3.2 and Table 3 notes; p. 18, Appendix C, equation C.1

confirmed.statement: HAT's 0.24 points/0.32 SDs, Training's 0.34 points/0.44 SDs, and comparison p-values .353, .690 and .166 match the text.
S1-O3/S2-O3 describe treatment-level dispersion of rated performance and potential payments: other and set are supported; the reported CV and Gini values all match Table 5.

S1-O4/S1-O5/S2-O4 score participant-produced words using GloVe semantic distances, not self-reports. automated_score and participant are supported, and testing occurred in the same session after Questionnaire II.

confirmed.statement: The HAT modified-DAT increase of 0.19 SDs is printed in the text. Figure 4b supports its positive interval and the reported nonsignificant DAT and Training results; it supplies no exact raw coefficient labels.

summary: Criterion 3 holds because independent evaluators rated participants' submitted ideas. The form misclassifies within-person DAT variety, asserts AI removal without explicit support, records approximate raw coefficients not numerically reported, and omits Table 8's two derived creativity outcomes.
